Hi Sara — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and our proposed next steps so everyone is aligned before engineering picks up the test work: 

Key SLOs we captured
- P95 latency target: 200ms for standard text-gen endpoints (non-streaming)
- Streaming sessions: sustain 75 concurrent streams with end-to-end p95 < 350ms for first byte of each chunk
- Throughput: peak 600 req/s sustained for 20 minute windows with 5 minute warmup
- Success criteria: <1% 5xx, token-level cost within expected envelope

Customer-led test asks from Redwood
- Please share the k6 or Locust scripts you plan to run (we can accept either). If you have separate streaming script (websocket/k6 + plugin), include both.
- Provide an account or token to hit our test cluster (we’ll give you the allowlist once we have IPs)
- Confirm a 3-hour window where you can run multiple ramps (proposed below)

Proposed test window (tentative)
- Tue Aug 24, 2027 — 09:00–12:00 PT (we can switch to Mon/Tue depending on your ops calendar)

Attachments: I’ve attached a short SLO summary with what Redwood will monitor during the run (umbratek-slo-summary.pdf).

Next steps
1) Sara — can you confirm the test window and share scripts?
2) Priyom/Ben — once Sara confirms, we’ll circulate Redwood egress IPs and create a test account; I’ll drop the temporary creds to Sara directly.
3) Vivek — tagging you for streaming guidance (warmup, KV cache priming, recommended ramp profile).

Thanks — talk soon,

Quick technical guidance for the group — streaming + concurrency specifics and a suggested load profile: 

Streaming considerations
- For streaming (websocket or SSE), prefer a dedicated runner that can maintain long-lived connections rather than firing short-lived HTTP requests. k6 with the websocket plugin works well; Locust with gevent is fine too.
- Important: prime the KV/prefix cache by running a short burst of representative prefix requests ~10 minutes before the main ramps. This avoids cold-cache p95 spikes.

Recommended ramp profile (3-hour window split)
- 09:00–09:10 — baseline verification (5-10% of target)
- 09:10–09:25 — warmup ramp to 40% (gradual increase)
- 09:25–10:00 — ramp to 100% of target (600 rps) and sustain for 30 minutes
- 10:00–10:20 — reduce to 50% and run streaming-focused scenarios for concurrency validation
- 10:20–11:00 — second 30m sustained peak with mixed payload sizes
- 11:00–12:00 — cooldown and targeted failure-injection tests (retry/backoff verification)

Metric hooks we’ll rely on
- p95 latency per route, 5xx rate, token throughput, concurrency counts, first-byte latency for streaming chunks.

Scripts attached: k6-streaming-sample.js (demonstrates websocket connect + chunk consumption), locustfile_streaming.py (hybrid HTTP + websocket tasks). For k6, ensure you set the header Authorization: Bearer <token> and x-redwood-test-account: umbratek-test-4723.

Let us know if you want Redwood to run the first ramp; happy to kick it off if you prefer a joint run.

—Vivek
Principal Inference Engineer, Redwood Inference
